en: One Scroll of the Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts.
Compiled by the Grand Master of State Affairs, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sui with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, Recipient of the Purple Robe, Posthumously Honored as Minister of Works, and Entitled Dajian (Great Mirror).
"We, the disciples [Name] and others, bow our heads in homage and take refuge before all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm;
before the teachings of Yoga and Dhāraṇī, and the assembly of the great Bodhisattvas."
And by paying homage to the bodhicitta, one can fulfill the accumulations of merit and wisdom and attain unsurpassed enlightenment; therefore, I prostrate in reverence.
The mantra for paying homage to the Buddha is as follows:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāmantraṇa-karomi. Next, one should perform mental offerings as follows:
"May this disciple [Name], and all others, offer every kind of worship throughout all lands in the ten directions—flower garlands, lamps, and fragrant unguents."
With food, drink, banners, pennants, and canopies, I sincerely offer these to you.
To all the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas, as well as all the worthy sages and saints,
I now pay homage with a most sincere heart.
The mantra for the Universal Offering to Ākāśagarbha is:
*Oṃ gaganasvabhāva vajra hūṃ*. Next, one should perform repentance:
"I, disciple [Name], and others, now before all Buddhas..."
O assembly of great bodhisattvas:
throughout the beginningless cycle of transmigration, up until this very day,
you have been deluded regarding the nature of true suchness and have given rise to false conceptualizations.
The unwholesome states of greed, hatred, and delusion; the afflictions of the three karmic paths and the secondary afflictions;
transgressions of the defeats (pārājika), as well as other faults and misdeeds;
and the slandering of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—[I confess all these].
Having plundered the property of the Triple Gem and extensively committed the crimes of the immediate retribution—
throughout immeasurable and boundless kalpas, beyond all calculation—
whether acting for oneself, inciting others to act, or seeing, hearing, or rejoicing in such deeds.
Furthermore, relying on the ultimate truth, the truly subtle principle,
one observes with the noble eye of wisdom that throughout the three periods of past, present, and future,
nothing at all can be apprehended; these are merely conceptual constructions created by one's own mind.
Because they are false and unreal, I take them as the skillful means of wisdom, equal as space.
I vow never again to conceal them; from this point forward, having already repented, I shall refrain.
I shall forever sever [these faults] and never commit them again; until I attain perfect awakening, I shall never transgress once more.
May the assembly of all Bodhisattvas, out of compassion, grant me their protection.
"May my karmic obstacles be extinguished; therefore, I pay homage with a sincere heart.
The mantra for repentance and the extinction of sins is:
"Oṃ sarvapāpānahaṃ vajrāya svāhā. Next, one should receive the Three Refuges:
"We, the disciples [Name], from this day forward,
take refuge in all the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the five wisdoms and three bodies;
we take refuge in the Vajrayāna, the Dharma of the true nature of self-essence."
I take refuge in the irreversible Bodhisattva Saṅgha of great compassion.
Having completed my refuge in the Triple Gem, I shall never again take refuge in paths of self-interest or false views; with a sincere heart, I now pay homage.
The mantra for the three refuges is:
"Oṃ bhuḥ khaṃ. Next, one should receive the bodhicitta vow:
"I, disciple [Name], and all others, before all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas..."
From this day forward, until I attain perfect enlightenment, I vow to give rise to the bodhicitta:
"Sentient beings are infinite; I vow to deliver them all. Merit and wisdom are infinite; I vow to accumulate them all."
I vow to study the boundless Buddha-dharma; I vow to serve the boundless Tathāgatas;
I vow to realize unsurpassed bodhi.
The awakening mind now generated is far removed from all natures and characteristics.
The aggregates, elements, and sense bases, along with the grasping subject and the grasped object—
all phenomena are entirely without self, equal to space.
One’s own mind is fundamentally unarisen, for emptiness is perfect peace.
"Just as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Have generated the great bodhicitta, I now generate it in this same way; Therefore, I pay homage with a sincere heart.
Next, recite the mantra for receiving the bodhicitta vow:

*Oṃ jñānamūrti svabhāvaviśuddha svāhā.* **The Text for Repentance upon Receiving the Bodhicitta Vow according to the Supreme Vehicle Teachings** “Disciples such as I, [name], take refuge in all the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, who take the Great Bodhicitta as their supreme guide, capable of leading us away from all evil realms and showing the way for humans and devas to enter Great Nirvāṇa. For this reason, we now prostrate with a sincere heart.”

"We, the disciples [Name] and others, offer all that is most excellent, sublime, and wondrous throughout the worlds of the ten directions—incense, flowers, banners, canopies, and various other offerings—to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
"I prostrate with a sincere heart.

We, the disciples [Name] and others, from the beginningless past until this very day, have been afflicted by various afflictions such as greed, anger, and ignorance, as well as secondary afflictions such as resentment and hatred, which have disturbed our bodies and minds. We have extensively committed all manner of unwholesome physical actions—killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying; unwholesome verbal actions—false speech, frivolous talk, harsh words, and divisive speech; and unwholesome mental actions—covetousness, malice, and wrong views."

Various afflictions have been continuously entangling and defiling their minds since beginningless time, causing them to commit immeasurable transgressions through body, speech, and mind—such as killing one's parents, killing an Arhat, shedding the blood of a Buddha, or causing schism in the Sangha;
slandering the Triple Gem, beating or binding sentient beings;
breaking the fast, violating the precepts, drinking alcohol, eating meat, and consuming the five pungent roots.
Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless, beyond the reach of memory or knowledge.
Today, with a sincere heart, I reveal and repent of them; having repented once, I shall forever sever their continuity and dare not commit them again.
“I only pray that all Buddhas of the ten directions and all great Bodhisattvas will empower and protect us with their mindfulness, so that our karmic obstacles and hindrances may be extinguished.

We, the disciples [Name] and others, from this present life until we sit at the site of enlightenment, throughout this interval, take refuge in the unsurpassed three bodies of the Tathāgata; we take refuge in the Dharma-treasury of the Vaipulya Mahāyāna; we take refuge in the assembly of all non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas.”
I have completed my refuge in the Buddha; I have completed my refuge in the Dharma; I have completed my refuge in the Sangha.
From this day forward, I shall no longer take refuge in the two vehicles or in non-Buddhist paths. I only pray that all Buddhas of the ten directions will bear witness to us.
"I prostrate with a sincere heart.
Disciples such as I, from this present body until we sit at the site of enlightenment, shall in the interval between them vow to give rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta."
Sentient beings are boundless; I vow to deliver them all. Merit and wisdom are boundless; I vow to accumulate them all.
Dharma gates are boundless; I vow to study them all. The Tathāgatas are boundless; I vow to serve them all.
Unsurpassed Bodhi; I vow to realize it.

“Now, regarding this resolve we have made, we shall further distance ourselves from the dualistic marks of self and phenomena (*ātma-dharma*), manifesting original enlightenment (*mūla-bodhi*). With the mirror-like wisdom (*ādarśa-jñāna*) of the equality of *tathatā* appearing before us, may we attain skillful wisdom and fully perfect the mind of Samantabhadra. We pray that all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions will bear witness to us.”

With a sincere heart, I pay homage: Namo to Akṣobhya Buddha of the East; Namo to Ratnasambhava Buddha of the South; Namo to Amitābha Buddha of the West; Namo to Amoghasiddhi Buddha of the North; Namo to Vairocana Buddha of the Pure Dharmakāya. The Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts, in one fascicle.
